meta.title: plan your house on your own computer
meta.description: Free, open-source house planner: 2D plans, 3D model, stairs, structure, roofs, utilities, finishes, costs and exports. Runs locally, no account, no tracking.
meta.og: Plan your house on your own computer. Open source, private, no account.
hero.title: Plan your house on your own computer.
hero.lead: Rooms, walls, stairs, roof, wiring and plumbing, finishes and costs, in 2D and 3D. Free and open source. No account, no cloud, no tracking: your house stays a file on your disk, with its full history.
hero.demoNote: The online demo runs in your browser with three sample houses, one of them a blank plot for your own idea. Move anything you like, but nothing is saved there: install the planner to keep your house.
hero.audience: For owners and self-builders at the idea stage, and for the architects and engineers they work with. Concept-level only: your architect and engineers sign the real project.

features.title: What it does
features.designItems: Rooms that tile each floor; drag walls and both sides follow
Any number of floors, basements and attics under the roof
Round rooms: bays, apses and towers with cone roofs
Doors, open passages, windows, terrace and sliding doors
Roofs: flat, mono-pitch, gable, hipped, mansard, roof terraces, dormers, chimneys; tiles, slate or zinc
Site: plot (any shape), drive and paths (curved), terrace, pool, garage, shed, greenhouse, carport, trees
features.checkItems: Stairs: risers, treads, width, a way in at the foot and out at the top; straight or U-shaped with winders; auto-fix
Structure: slab spans between load-bearing walls, walls with nothing underneath
Overlaps, gaps, windows that lost their wall, floors with nothing below
One list of everything that needs attention, one click to jump to it
features.fitItems: Floor and wall finishes, tiles with your own photos, tile zones and quantities
Electrical (230/400 V), water, drainage and gas points generated from the appliances, with circuits and loads
Facade: colours, shutters, surrounds, cornice, corner stones, Juliet balconies
features.shareItems: Cost estimate from the plan's own quantities, against your budget, in any currency (ECB rates)
Printable sheets at true scale (PDF), 3D views, DXF for CAD, a handover brief for your architect, CSV costs
Comments on any room, wall or window, kept as text files
Every save is a git commit: full history of each house, undo anything
how.title: How it works
how.p1: The planner is a small web app that runs on localhost. Each house is a folder with one house.json (the whole design), your comments as Markdown files, and its own git history. Put the folder in Dropbox, iCloud, Google Drive or OneDrive to keep it backed up and on all your computers.
how.p2: Because the design is a plain, documented file, you can read it, diff it, script it, or let an AI assistant change it for you.
install.title: Install
install.need: You need Node.js 20 or newer and git (both free, for Windows, macOS and Linux).
install.open: Open http://localhost:3000. Start from the example family house, the small manor with a tower, or an empty plot.
install.cloudTitle: Keep your houses in a cloud folder
install.cloudText: Point the planner at any folder, for example a synced drive:
install.cloudMore: or copy planner.config.example.json to planner.config.json and set housesDir. On Windows PowerShell: $env:HOUSES_DIR="$HOME\Dropbox\houses"; npm start.
install.updateText: Your houses are not part of the app's folder history, so updating never touches them.
use.title: How to use it
use.steps: Rooms. Click + Room, drag rooms into place, drag a wall to move it (the rooms on both sides follow), or type exact sizes in the side panel. Everything snaps to 25 cm and to nearby walls.
Openings. Select a room and add doors, open passages and windows. Drag them along the wall; drag their ends to make them wider.
Floors and stairs. Add a floor above or a basement, place a staircase and a void above it. The stairs check tells you if it fits and offers to fix it.
Roof and facade. The roof follows the building by itself; pick its shape and covering, add terraces, dormers and chimneys, and the facade details you like.
Fit out. Add furniture and appliances, then Generate utilities for sockets, lights, water, drains and circuits. Choose floor and wall finishes.
Check and price. Look at the issues list and the Costs tab; set your budget and replace the example prices with your builder's quotes.
Share. Export printable sheets, DXF and the handover brief for your architect, engineers and installers.
ai.title: Work with an AI assistant
ai.p1: The repository is written to be read by AI coding assistants. CLAUDE.md documents the data model and the rules, so an assistant such as Claude Code can change your house safely, run the same checks the app runs, and commit each change to your house's history.
ai.steps: In the planner, select a room or wall and write a comment: "Make the kitchen 1 m longer and move the island."
In your terminal, in the planner's folder, run the assistant and type /apply-comments.
Each comment is applied, checked, committed and marked resolved. Reload the planner to see it.
ai.p2: You can also ask for whole designs: "Draft a 3-bedroom house for about 200k, with the master suite on the ground floor", or "Build this catalogue house: <link>". Always review what it did; every step can be undone from the history.
help.title: Help wanted: experts, testers and translators
help.p1: The checks, rules and example prices are deliberately simple and certainly wrong in places. If you are an architect, structural engineer, electrician, plumber, heating or energy specialist, or cost estimator, you can make this tool safer and more useful for people planning their homes all over the world, without writing code:
help.items: Tell us which rules are wrong or missing for your country (stairs, spans, circuits, drainage, ventilation…).
Check the example prices for your region.
Review the printable sheets and the handover brief: what would you need to receive from a client?
Try it on a real project and tell us where it gets in the way.
help.devs: Developers are very welcome too: the app is plain JavaScript with no build step and one dependency (Three.js). Read CONTRIBUTING.md, pick an issue, open a pull request. Every change is reviewed by the maintainer before it is merged.
help.translate: Speak another language? Translating this page is one file: copy site/i18n/en.json to your language code and open a pull request.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.text: The planner runs only on your computer and talks to nobody, except when you ask it to download currency exchange rates from the European Central Bank. This page sets no cookies, loads nothing from other sites and counts nobody.
permit.title: Not a permit document
permit.text: The planner helps you think and talk about your house. Its checks are rules of thumb, not building codes. An authorised architect and engineers must design and sign the real project.
